chapters.body: He left Pellow Freight, studied full time, moved to Millbrook and passed CAF 1 with 61.
chapters.title: The resit months

chapters.body: Omar left for Dubai, Law was dropped, and the phone habit came back without the gym.
chapters.title: Settling in Millbrook

chapters.body: Power cuts, a UPS, and a steady push through Sir Waqas's lectures.
chapters.title: The Tax push

conversations.summary: He scrolls his phone in bed past midnight most nights, then is late and foggy for work at Pellow Freight; his manager Mrs. Danvers has noticed him arriving late.
conversations.title: Can't sleep again

conversations.summary: He is studying for the CAF qualification to move beyond his accounts assistant job; first paper CAF 1 Financial Accounting on 8 December; manages about an hour of study after work.
conversations.title: Why CAF

conversations.summary: His sister Hina in Islamabad calls every Sunday and backs his CAF plan; he feels she is the one in the family who understands it.
conversations.title: Hina's call

conversations.summary: His mother worries about money and the cost of the exams; he pays each paper's fee (about 15,000) from his salary.
conversations.title: Money worries

conversations.summary: The day after sitting CAF 1 he felt the consolidation question went badly and he ran out of time on the last two questions.
conversations.title: After the exam

conversations.summary: He failed CAF 1 with 46 (pass 50) and decided to resit in June, practising past papers under time.
conversations.title: Result day

conversations.summary: He joined Ironline gym near the office and plans to go before work on Monday, Wednesday and Friday at 6:30.
conversations.title: Starting the gym

conversations.summary: Three weeks into the gym; on gym days he sleeps before midnight, and the gym has helped his phone-in-bed habit more than app blockers did.
conversations.title: Gym is working

conversations.summary: He resigned from Pellow Freight (last day 31 March) to study full time for the June resit on about 120,000 of savings; Mrs. Danvers was kind and left the door open.
conversations.title: Quitting Pellow

conversations.summary: His left knee hurts and swells after squats; he booked the physio Dr. Saleh.
conversations.title: Knee pain

conversations.summary: Dr. Saleh ruled out squats and running for two months (patellar tendon), so he stopped the gym and switched to a 20-minute daily walk.
conversations.title: Physio verdict

conversations.summary: Studying full time from 9 to 4 at the Model Town library, where he focuses far better than at home.
conversations.title: Library routine

conversations.summary: His friend Omar, also resitting CAF 1 in June, does past papers with him on Thursdays at the library; it keeps him accountable.
conversations.title: Omar study buddy

conversations.summary: The family is moving from the Kestrel Road flat to his aunt Khala Rukhsana's house in Millbrook after another rent rise; he will have the quiet rooftop room.
conversations.title: Moving to Millbrook

conversations.summary: After the move he studies in the rooftop room from 5:30 to 8 am before the heat, with his best focus ever; the library is now 90 minutes away by bus.
conversations.title: Rooftop mornings

conversations.summary: Four days before the resit he had done eleven timed past papers, scores rising from 44 to 58.
conversations.title: Resit nerves

conversations.summary: He passed the CAF 1 resit with 61; Omar passed with 55 and is moving to Dubai for a job.
conversations.title: Passed

conversations.summary: He planned to sit CAF 5 Tax and CAF 3 Law together in December; Sir Waqas's online Tax course has 60 recorded lectures.
conversations.title: Next papers

conversations.summary: The phone-in-bed habit is back since the gym stopped; he scrolls till 2 am and loses his rooftop mornings to the heat.
conversations.title: Phone again

conversations.summary: He dropped CAF 3 Law to sit only CAF 5 Tax in December, with Sir Waqas's agreement.
conversations.title: Dropping Law

conversations.summary: He missed the 20 August exam form deadline because of an evening power cut and a bank website outage; the late fee is 3,000.
conversations.title: Missed the form

conversations.summary: He started a focus on stopping phone use in bed; first idea is charging the phone in the kitchen from 11 pm.
conversations.title: Focus: phone in bed

conversations.summary: First week of charging the phone in the kitchen: asleep by midnight four nights of seven; failures came from taking the phone back 'for the alarm'.
conversations.title: Kitchen charger works

conversations.summary: Load shedding returned (two hours most evenings, sometimes mornings), which stops his lectures because the router goes off.
conversations.title: Power cuts

conversations.summary: He paid the Tax exam fee, 18,000 including the 3,000 late fee, which upset his mother; plans a small UPS for the router.
conversations.title: Paid the fee

conversations.summary: He bought a router UPS for 9,500, giving about three hours of internet; did two lectures during an evening power cut for the first time.
conversations.title: Bought the UPS

conversations.summary: Omar called from Dubai (long hours, saving well); he misses their Thursday study sessions and finds studying alone lonelier.
conversations.title: Omar in Dubai

conversations.summary: He is at Tax lecture 31 of 60 with the exam on 1 December and Sir Waqas's advice to finish lectures by end of November; Tuesdays go badly because of family visits.
conversations.title: Behind on lectures

letters.body: Three evenings lost to power cuts, and still eight lectures. The kitchen charger held five nights.
letters.title: The week the lights went out

letters.body: The UPS changed the evenings: two lectures during a cut for the first time.
letters.title: A box that keeps the router on

letters.body: Every Tuesday this month ended at zero; the other days averaged close to two.
letters.title: Tuesdays

messages.text: It's almost midnight and I'm still scrolling reels in bed. Tomorrow I have to be at Pellow Freight by nine.
This happens every night. I tell myself ten minutes and it's suddenly 2 am.
Mrs. Danvers already noticed I came in late twice last week.
I want to finish CAF so I'm not stuck as an accounts assistant forever.
My first paper is CAF 1 Financial Accounting, the exam is on 8 December.
Studying after work is hard, I only manage maybe an hour on good days.
Hina called from Islamabad, she always calls on Sundays. She said she believes I'll pass.
She's the only one in the family who gets why I'm doing this.
Ammi keeps asking how much the exams cost. She worries about money all the time.
Each paper's fee is around 15,000 and I pay it from my salary.
The CAF 1 exam was yesterday. The consolidation question destroyed me.
I think I ran out of time on the last two questions.
Result came. 46 in CAF 1. Pass is 50. I missed by four marks.
I want to resit in June and this time actually do past papers under time.
I joined Ironline gym near the office, going before work at 6:30.
The plan is three mornings a week, Monday Wednesday Friday.
Three weeks of gym now. On gym days I actually sleep before midnight because I'm tired.
Funny how the gym fixed my phone-in-bed problem more than any app blocker.
Sana and I ended it tonight. I don't want this remembered.
We'd been together two years.
I handed in my notice at Pellow Freight today. Last day is 31 March.
Mrs. Danvers was kind about it, she said come back if it doesn't work out.
I'll study full time until the resit and live on my savings, about 120,000.
My left knee hurts after squats. It's been swelling since Tuesday.
I'll see a physio, Dr. Saleh, on Monday.
Dr. Saleh says no squats or running for two months. Patellar tendon thing.
So the gym is basically over for now. I'll walk instead, twenty minutes a day.
Full-time study, day 5. I go to the Model Town library at 9 and stay till 4.
I focus way better at the library than at home, home has too many interruptions.
Omar and I are doing past papers together on Thursdays at the library.
He's sitting CAF 1 in June too. Having him there keeps me honest.
We're moving to Khala Rukhsana's house in Millbrook. The Kestrel Road flat rent went up again.
I'll get the small room on the roof. It's quiet up there.
Since the move I study on the roof from 5:30 to 8 before it gets hot. Best focus I've ever had.
The library is too far from Millbrook now, ninety minutes by bus.
Resit is in four days. I've done eleven past papers under time.
My scores went from 44 to 58 across them.
I PASSED. 61 in CAF 1.
Omar passed too, 55. He's moving to Dubai next week for a job though.
Next I'm doing CAF 5 Tax and CAF 3 Law together in December.
Sir Waqas teaches Tax online, his course has 60 recorded lectures.
I'm back to scrolling in bed till 2. Without the gym I'm never tired at night.
Mornings on the roof are ruined, I wake up at 9 and it's already too hot.
Two papers at once is too much. I'm dropping Law, just Tax in December.
Sir Waqas agreed, he said Tax alone is plenty for one sitting.
I missed the exam form deadline on the 20th. There was a power cut all evening and the bank site was down.
Late fee is 3,000 extra. So annoying.
I want to properly fix the phone thing this time, not just try for a few days.
Idea: phone charges in the kitchen from 11 pm.
Week one of the kitchen charger. Slept by 12 four nights out of seven.
The nights it failed were when I took the phone 'just for an alarm'.
Load shedding is back, two hours every evening, sometimes in the morning too.
When the power goes, the lectures stop because the router dies.
Paid the Tax exam fee today, 18,000 with the late fee. Ammi was upset about the extra 3,000.
I'm going to buy a small UPS for the router so power cuts don't stop lectures.
Got the UPS for 9,500. Router stays on for about three hours now.
Did two lectures during the evening cut for the first time.
Omar video called from Dubai. He says the job is long hours but he's saving well.
I miss our Thursday sessions, studying alone is lonelier.
I'm at lecture 31 of 60 and the exam is 1 December. Sir Waqas said finish lectures by end of November.
Tuesdays are always bad because Khala's family visits.
Plan for today: two lectures before noon if the power holds, then nap after Zuhr.
Good plan. Two lectures before noon, nap after Zuhr, practice questions on paper if the power goes.
If the power goes I'll do the practice questions on paper instead.
That's a solid fallback.
Lectures 32 and 33 are both on sales tax.
Sales tax it is. Tell me how it goes.
